import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_16/training_8.csv",
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    # index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per instructions
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# UNION all source tables (concatenate)
union_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types
# Target schema: ['created_at': string, 'text': string, 'coordinates': string, 'hashtags': string]

# Convert all columns to string type (including NaNs to 'nan' string)
# But from examples, coordinates can be NaN (float NaN), hashtags is list or empty list.
# We will convert coordinates NaN to string 'nan' to match target type string.
# For hashtags, convert list/dict to string representation as in target examples hashtags column is string type.

# Convert 'created_at' and 'text' to string
union_df['created_at'] = union_df['created_at'].astype(str)
union_df['text'] = union_df['text'].astype(str)

# For 'coordinates', convert NaN to string 'nan', else convert to string
union_df['coordinates'] = union_df['coordinates'].apply(lambda x: 'nan' if pd.isna(x) else str(x))

# For 'hashtags', the source sometimes has empty list [] or list of dicts.
# We convert the hashtags column to string representation of the list (like "[]" or "[{'text': 'Melmetal', 'indices': [21, 30]}]")
# This matches the target schema string type.
union_df['hashtags'] = union_df['hashtags'].apply(lambda x: str(x) if not pd.isna(x) else '[]')

# Reorder columns to target schema order
Target9_16 = union_df[['created_at', 'text', 'coordinates', 'hashtags']]

# Write the final target table to the specified path without the index column
Target9_16.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
